summary.en: U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth travelled to Caracas and signed a new military partnership with the interim Venezuelan government, expanding cooperation to target drug trafficking and designating Venezuela a compliant security partner while meeting interim president and Delcy Rodriguez. The United States also launched a Caribbean operation during which a marine died after falling overboard. The agreement broadens security engagement beyond earlier bilateral ties. Two battle-related deaths occurred in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: U.S. forsvarsminister Pete Hegseth reiste til Caracas og signerte et nytt militært partnerskap med den midlertidige venezuelanske regjeringen, og utvidet samarbeidet for å bekjempe narkotikasmugling og betegnet Venezuela som en etterfølgende sikkerhetspartner mens han møtte den midlertidige presidenten og Delcy Rodriguez. USA lanserte også en karibisk operasjon der en marine døde etter å ha falt overbord. Avtalen utvider sikkerhetsengasjementet utover tidligere bilaterale bånd. To dødsfall i kamp ble registrert i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro as well as Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
